subject: POC plan, success criteria & risk tracking
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-analytics.com>, James O'Connor <james.oconnor@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: POC plan, success criteria & risk tracking

Thanks again for your time today — good call. Per our discussion, here's a concise recap, proposed POC plan, and the risks we should track so we can move quickly next week. Please confirm or flag anything missing.

Recap / objectives:
- Goal: Validate Redwood for production retrieval + semantic search on your customer support corpus (approx 15M tokens).
- Primary success criteria:
  1) Precision@10 >= 82% on your evaluation set (we'll use the sample you shared).
  2) 95th percentile latency for retrieval+generation < 800ms for 1k concurrent sessions in our dedicated config.
  3) End-to-end throughput to support your SLA (approx 30 reqs/s).

Proposed 2-week POC timeline (target start Mon Mar 15):
- Week 1: Data ingestion + baseline runs (owner: Acme / Dev for ingestion).
- Week 2: Tuning, expanded load tests, canary with subset of traffic (owner: Redwood / Aditya + Dev).

Immediate next steps (action owners):
- Acme: Confirm sample dataset and SOC2 access artifact requirements (Samantha) — due Thu Mar 12.
- Redwood: Share POC plan spreadsheet and roles (attached) — Marissa/Aditya (attached: 20260310-poc-plan.xlsx).
- Redwood SE: Stand up test endpoint & provide ingestion guide (Dev) — target Mon Mar 15.

Risk/issue tracking (initial):
- Data connectivity: need S3 credentials or secure file upload (blocking). Owner: Acme/Dev.
- Tokenization mismatch on support data -> may cause precision drop. Mitigation: pre-tokenization script + sampling. Owner: Dev/Acme.
- Query timeouts under concurrent load. Mitigation: tuned batching + autoscale policy. Owner: Aditya/Redwood infra.

Escalation path: If a blocking bug is found during baseline we will: 1) open internal P0 ticket, 2) notify Lukas (engineering lead), 3) schedule an immediate triage call. Expected initial response SLA: 4 business hours.

Attachment: 20260310-poc-plan.xlsx (POC milestones, owners, success criteria).

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, James O'Connor <james.oconnor@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 17:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC plan, success criteria & risk tracking

Thanks Marissa — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A couple of clarifications / constraints from our side: 

1) Data access: we cannot provide raw S3 creds. Procurement would prefer an ephemeral signed URL or a secure upload. I looped procurement in (procurement@acme-analytics.com).
2) Feature note: our search relies on custom embeddings we compute in-house. We'll need either the ability to bring embeddings or to run ``text-embedding`` using Redwood. If we bring embeddings, we need assurances on input format.
3) Security: we need a short doc on data retention and SOC2 evidence before we start ingesting any sample data.

On blockers: the data access approach is the biggest gating item for week 1. If we can't arrange a secure transfer, we may need to delay.

We can confirm the sample dataset by Thu. Also happy to do a 30-min tech sync Thu morning with Dev to walk through ingestion options.

Best,
Samantha
Head of Data Platforms | Acme Analytics
samantha.lee@acme-analytics.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-analytics.com>, James O'Connor <james.oconnor@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC plan, success criteria & risk tracking

Appreciate the speed, Samantha. Quick responses below and proposed mitigations: 

- Secure transfer: We can support pre-signed S3 URLs (time-limited) or a one-time secure upload to our ingestion portal. We'll treat the sample as restricted access. Dev — I'll ask you to share the upload link + steps in the Friday tech sync.
- Embeddings: Either approach is fine. If Acme brings embeddings, please use our CSV schema (we'll share). If you want Redwood to compute, we'll run embeddings in a private job (we can set retention to zero for the job).
- SOC2 / data retention: Attaching our latest terms and SOC2 summary (redwood_terms_v2.pdf). If you need a longer package, we can schedule a compliance call.

I'll pencil in a Thu 10:00 AM PST tech sync with Dev. Dev, can you confirm availability and prep an ingestion checklist and the pre-tokenization script?

Marissa
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-analytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC plan, success criteria & risk tracking

Hi all — quick technical update after prototyping ingestion with a 100k-sample. Two items to flag: 

1) Blocking bug observed: when ingesting certain multi-line transcripts with legacy punctuation, the runtime tokenizer (v3.1.2) can produce a wrong token boundary that leads to a downstream embedding mismatch. Repro steps: ingest sample file "support_sample_multiline.jsonl" -> run embedding job -> observe token count mismatch. Screenshot attached.
- Impact: For some queries, similarity scoring degrades by ~10-12 percentage points versus expected baseline. This affects Precision@10 metric.
- Proposed short-term mitigation: run our pre-tokenization script (attached in the Drive link) to normalize line breaks and punctuation before embedding. This reduces the mismatch for the majority of cases.

2) Data transfer: I can generate a secure upload link and a short ingestion checklist (CSV schema + max row size). I will also provide a small helper script to convert your embeddings into our CSV schema if you choose to bring them.

If the tokenizer bug shows up on your full sample, I recommend we open an internal engineering P0 ticket. Lukas — tagging you in case we need a patch or advice on whether a runtime patch is required before canary.

Attachment referenced: screenshot_bug_502.png (runtime token boundary). See Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cPOC

I'll be on the Thu tech sync and will bring the checklist.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: James O'Connor <james.oconnor@acme-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC plan, success criteria & risk tracking

Thanks for the update, Dev — appreciate the playbook. Two quick asks from our side: 

1) Can we do a small canary with 100k rows first after the pre-tokenization to validate the mitigation? If that looks good we'll scale to the full corpus.
2) Data retention & compliance: we'll review the attached terms; if acceptable we'll proceed. If not, we'll ask for a short compliance call.

If the tokenizer issue requires a runtime patch, what is the expected turnaround for a hotfix? We need to understand potential delays to the 2-week timeline.

James

Subject: Re: POC plan, success criteria & risk tracking

Follow-up and confirmed next steps after the tech sync this morning: 

1) Canary run: Acme will upload a 100k-row sample via the secure upload flow by Mon Mar 15. Dev will validate ingestion and run pre-tokenization. Target: results back by Tue Mar 16 EOD.
2) If precision is within target after mitigation (Precision@10 >= 82%), we proceed to full ingestion and load testing during Week 2.
3) If the tokenizer bug persists on the canary, we will escalate: 
   - Marissa/Aditya open an internal P0 ticket (POC-2026-34) and assign to Lukas for triage.
   - Expected initial engineering response: within 4 business hours.
   - Contingency: we can run the POC using Redwood's managed embedding compute (avoiding local embedding differences) if a patch will take >48 hours.

Action owners recap: 
- Acme (Samantha/James): upload 100k sample via secure upload by Mon Mar 15.
- Dev: ingest, apply pre-tokenization, run canary tests, report results Tue Mar 16 EOD.
- Marissa/Aditya: monitor results, open P0 ticket if needed, coordinate escalation.
